Act as the implementation sub-agent for this task.

Repo indkhan/Moneo. GitHub issue #241 part 2 (read `gh issue view 241`, and AGENTS.md, especially the Non-negotiables on cards and the organizer exception). Part 1 (PR #290) is merged: `lib/database.types.ts` is generated, and `serviceDb()`, `createClient()` and `Db` (`lib/database.ts`) are typed with `Database`.

Owner's decision for this part: read-only client types for AI tools; writes only via accepted cards (proposal application) and the organizer's labeling (`organized_by = 'ai'`, undoable).

Do this:
1. Inventory every place AI-driven code gets a database client: chat tools (`app/api/chat/route.ts`, `lib/ai/`), voice (`lib/ai/voice-*`), artifacts, background agents (`lib/ai/agent-*`, `workflows/`), `lib/finance/finance-context.ts` (`FinanceContext.supabase`). Classify each use as read, card application (`lib/ai/agent-apply.ts` and friends), organizer labeling, or other legitimate app write. Put the table in the PR body with counts.
2. Add a type, e.g. `ReadonlyDb` in `lib/database.ts`, derived from the generated `Database` so that `.from(t)` exposes only `select` (no `insert/update/upsert/delete`) and `.rpc(name)` accepts only RPCs explicitly listed as read-only (a typed allowlist; mutating RPCs are classified explicitly, not exposed by an unrestricted rpc escape hatch). Prefer a pure type-level narrowing over a runtime wrapper; if a runtime wrapper is simpler and safer, say why.
3. Make AI tool contexts take `ReadonlyDb`, so a read-only AI tool cannot compile a direct table mutation or a mutating RPC. Card application and the organizer get the full client through their own narrow entry points. Don't remove legitimate app writes.
4. Add a type test (e.g. `// @ts-expect-error` is a comment, so use `expectTypeOf` from vitest, or a `.test-d.ts` checked by typecheck) proving a mutation through `ReadonlyDb` fails to compile and a select compiles. Add or extend tests for apply authorization, scope revocation and duplicate application only where none exist yet (check first; extend rather than duplicate).
5. Add an AGENTS.md rules-table row naming what enforces it.

Behaviour must not change. Create branch `t3/issue-241-readonly-ai-db` from origin/main. Commit in steps with plain messages ending with "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>". Before opening the PR, merge origin/main again (another PR is editing lib/finance for noUncheckedIndexedAccess; keep main's changes on conflicts). Run `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` yourself and quote their last lines. Tests use only the moneo-qa test backend; never the owner's backend (.env, Docker project `moneo`, port 3000). Never run `qa:reset` or `docker compose -p moneo-qa down`; if you apply anything to moneo-qa, revert it without CASCADE. Real AI calls cost money: mock them. Never kill a process you didn't start (verify by PID). Don't end your turn while a command is still running. No comments in code. Open the PR (body ends with "🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)" and "Closes #241"), never merge it. Final line: PR <full URL>, head <SHA>.

**Priority:** P1 (correctness, security or verification priority).

## Problem and current evidence

The audit found ungenerated database boundaries, 27 as unknown as casts and roughly 100 lib/ai write call sites without a type separation between tool reads and proposal application. These counts need rechecking. AI organizer category/merchant labels are the explicitly authorized exception to cards.

## Scope

Generate types from the migrated disposable QA database and make regeneration reproducible. Adopt them at database boundaries, replacing unsafe casts with validation or correctly typed queries. Separate read-only AI tool access from accepted-card write capabilities and the organizer's narrowly scoped, undoable labeling capability. Inventory chat, voice, artifacts and background agents; do not globally remove legitimate app writes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A read-only AI tool cannot compile a direct table mutation or mutating RPC call.
- [ ] Mutating RPCs are classified explicitly rather than exposed by an unrestricted rpc escape hatch.
- [ ] Financial writes still require accepted cards; organizer labels retain AI attribution and undo.
- [ ] Tests cover apply authorization, scope revocation and duplicate application.
- [ ] Generated types match migrations and work with both Docker and bundled desktop Postgres.

## Verification and constraints

Reproduce the current behaviour before changing it. Run the smallest relevant check during implementation, then npm test, npm run lint and npm run typecheck; add a build for app/config changes and real QA browser verification for changed user flows. Use only disposable moneo-qa services, synthetic records and mocked paid integrations. Verify source installation and desktop compatibility. Preserve financial history, corrections and undo. Do not add prose or comments in place of a deterministic boundary.

## Delivery

This issue records follow-up work; it does not claim the change is implemented. Recheck current main and #224 before starting, since the audit counts may have changed. Keep the PR focused and link its checks and relevant evidence here.
